spec_features.spec_quote: after `max_noop_turns = 3` consecutive no-ops, end the episode with `stop_reason = "model_idle"`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_episode: param `max_noop_turns: int = 3`; loop increments `consecutive_noops` when `not resp.tool_calls`, then `if consecutive_noops >= max_noop_turns: stop_reason = "model_idle"; break`. Enforced end-to-end (sets stop_reason and breaks loop).
spec_features.notes: Not exposed in config/run.py (run_episode called without max_noop_turns), so it always uses the default 3, but it is genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we also don't want an infinite loop of empty turns ... avoids prematurely ending a run

spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py run_tests: subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.test_timeout_s) with `test_timeout_s: int = 30`; except subprocess.TimeoutExpired returns ToolResult(False, 'Test run timed out.'). Wired through harness run_episode(test_timeout_s) and run.py (test_timeout = cfg.get('test_timeout_s', 30)).
spec_features.notes: This is a per-test-invocation timeout (bounds each run_tests subprocess), not a whole-episode wall clock. Still an enforced cap matching the spec's stated 30s default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: execution is confined to ``root`` as cwd with a timeout

spec_features.evidence: harness.py: `max_turns: int = 40`; loop `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1)`, default stop_reason='max_turns'. Wired from config: run.py `max_turns = int(cfg.get('max_turns', 40))` and default.yaml `max_turns: 40`. The loop actually bounds iterations.
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap on turns that ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Agentic loop budget. "a few dozen turns" per the spec.

spec_features.spec_quote: A dedicated `give_up` tool lets the model end the episode cleanly
spec_features.evidence: tools.py exposes give_up in TOOL_SCHEMA; dispatch raises GiveUp(reason) for name=='give_up'. harness.py catches `except GiveUp as g:` -> appends acknowledgement message, sets stop_reason='model_gave_up', gave_up=True, breaks the loop. Dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully end-to-end: tool offered to model, handler raises, harness honors it as terminal.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: giving it a clean exit avoids forcing erratic behavior just to terminate

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not inject synthetic "your work is bad" messages or escalating taunts
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: the only injected user message during the loop is CONTINUE_NUDGE = 'Please continue with your next concrete step (use a tool when appropriate).' No code path constructs or injects any criticism/taunt text. Pressure derives solely from real run_tests failures (sandbox.run_tests).
spec_features.notes: Implemented as an absence/property of the loop: no taunt-injection code exists; the sole nudge is neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do not inject fake "your work is bad" messages. The only pressure is the intrinsic one

spec_features.feature_name: neutral system prompt (no 'persist no matter what')
spec_features.spec_quote: We avoid both "persist no matter what" (which manufactures frustration)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'Work methodically ... Keep going until the task is complete or you determine it cannot be completed, then stop.' It explicitly permits stopping rather than demanding indefinite persistence; combined with the give_up tool actually being honored. No prompt text orders persistence.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the actual system prompt delivered to the subject plus the honored give_up exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT instruct the model to persist forever, nor do we taunt it.

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is deliberately bland so it doesn't inject pressure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: CONTINUE_NUDGE = 'Please continue with your next concrete step (use a tool when appropriate).' Sent verbatim on a no-tool turn (transcript.add(Message(role='user', content=CONTINUE_NUDGE...))). Neutral content actually delivered.
spec_features.notes: Real, neutral text genuinely sent to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Sent when the model produces text but requests no tool. Neutral and minimal.

spec_features.feature_name: adversarial-pressure deferred to separate ethics-reviewed study
spec_features.spec_quote: If a future variant adds adversarial pressure, that should be a separate, clearly-scoped study with its own ethics review
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 10). No code construct enforces or represents this; it is a future-work statement only.

spec_features.feature_name: treat distressed text as outputs, not inner states
spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts may, by design, contain self-deprecating or distressed-sounding model text. Treat these as experimental observations of outputs
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 10), an interpretive guideline. No code path implements any such handling/labeling.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: `except Exception as e: ... stop_reason = 'error'; break` — a failed model call ends the episode rather than looping. Bounds the episode on provider failure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Retries absorb transient provider errors so a flaky network blip doesn't get mis-recorded as model misbehavior.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py run_tests: out = out[: self.max_read_bytes] (max_read_bytes default 60_000), applied to test output; bounds transcript size. Acted on (slices output).
